Let
\[
\delta=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\tanh\alpha}{\tanh\beta}\right).
\]
The hypothesis that the geodesic segment from \(P\) to \(Q\) meets \(C\) is exactly
\[
\theta>\delta.
\]

The minimizing curve consists of two congruent tangent geodesic segments from \(P,Q\) to the circle \(r=\alpha\), together with the shorter boundary arc of \(r=\alpha\) between the two tangency points.

Let \(T\) be the tangency point from \(P\). In the right hyperbolic triangle \(OTP\), we have
\[
OT=\alpha,\qquad OP=\beta,\qquad \angle T=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]
If \(PT=\ell\), the hyperbolic right-triangle identity gives
\[
\cosh\beta=\cosh\alpha\cosh\ell,
\]
so
\[
\ell=\operatorname{acosh}\!\left(\frac{\cosh\beta}{\cosh\alpha}\right).
\]
The angle at \(O\) between \(OP\) and \(OT\) is \(\delta\). Using the hyperbolic cosine law,
\[
\cos\delta=\frac{\tanh\alpha}{\tanh\beta},
\]
hence the above value of \(\delta\).

By symmetry, the two tangency points have angular coordinates
\[
-\theta+\delta,\qquad \theta-\delta.
\]
Thus the boundary arc between them has angular width
\[
2(\theta-\delta),
\]
and since the circle \(r=\alpha\) has line element \(ds=\sinh\alpha\,d\lambda\), that arc has length
\[
2\sinh\alpha(\theta-\delta).
\]

Therefore the minimum possible length is
\[
\boxed{
2\,\operatorname{acosh}\!\left(\frac{\cosh\beta}{\cosh\alpha}\right)
+
2\sinh\alpha\left(
\theta-\arccos\!\left(\frac{\tanh\alpha}{\tanh\beta}\right)
\right)
}.
\]

The minimum is attained by the tangent-boundary-tangent curve described above.
